My final answer is in `final.py`. It scores **0.5631 on the search split**, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline, and I used **18 of the 24 scorer calls**.

**How it works:** the cache runs five eviction policies side by side on simulated copies of the cache. Every request goes through all of them, but only the real cache's hits count. The real cache copies whichever policy has had the most recent hits:
- On a miss, it stores the key only if that leading policy would store it.
- It then evicts a key the leading policy doesn't hold.
- Each policy's recent hits are halved every 2×capacity requests to track the trend. Another policy takes over only when it beats the current one by more than 5%, so the cache doesn't switch back and forth.

The five policies are four versions of W-TinyLFU and plain LRU. W-TinyLFU keeps a small recency area for new keys and only lets one into the main cache if it has been requested more often than the key it would push out. The four versions differ in two settings:
- the size of the new-key area (1% or 20% of capacity);
- how quickly old request counts fade (halved every 5, 20 or 100 × capacity requests).

| trace | hit rate |
|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.248 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.665 |
| phases | 0.640 |
| mixed | 0.281 |
| recency | 0.845 |
| shifting_loops | 0.699 |

**What I tried along the way:**
- A single W-TinyLFU with a self-tuning new-key area reached 0.50–0.53. With the area fixed at 1% it got 0.531.
- Following the best of several policies raised that to 0.544, then 0.553 after adding the 5% margin. Adding policies whose counts fade more slowly brought it to 0.563.
- Adding an ARC policy, a 50% new-key area or faster-fading counts changed nothing. Changing the switching timing or the margin made it worse.
- One test run had a tie-breaking bug and scored 0.421. I fixed it and re-ran it, so it cost one extra call.

The final score comes from traces I haven't seen, so expect some difference from 0.563. A few extra files from testing are still in the folder (`wtlfu.py`, `v_*.py`, `ex*.py`, `experts.py`, `arconly.py`, and `gen.py`, which builds made-up local test traces). They don't affect `final.py`.
